commits.subject: core: TExternalProcess compiles with the Delphi Linux compiler - see #648
commits.body:
THandle is unsigned on Delphi POSIX: the descriptors of TExternalProcess are
now an integer on POSIX, as CloseValid() and their checks against -1 expect.
RunSearchPath() casts its PAnsiChar argument for PosChar().

Tested with Delphi 13 for Linux64 on Debian 11: _RunRedirect and
_TExternalProcess pass.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: TExternalProcess and RunRedirect() on Delphi POSIX - see #648
commits.body:
mormot.core.os.delphi.pas now publishes the fppipe, fpdup2, fpfcntl,
fpwaitpid, wifexited, wexitstatus, fpsigemptyset, fpsigprocmask and
fpsigaction wrappers, with the TFilDes, TSigSet and SigactionRec types, so
that the POSIX code of TExternalProcess and RunRedirect() is no longer FPC-only.
On Linux, Delphi calls pipe2() from libc. close_range() is called on FPC only:
libc close_range() needs glibc 2.34, so Delphi uses the closing loop, up to the
highest opened descriptor. MaxDescriptors() now calls GetFileOpenLimit().
The child process zero-fills its sigaction record for SIG_DFL, since the
handler field name of the Delphi record depends on the platform.
The regression tests are compiled on Delphi POSIX too, except the SIGUSR1
sender of _RunRedirect, for the same reason.
Not compiled yet with a Delphi POSIX compiler.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: TExternalProcess resolves the Windows attribute list API at startup - see #648
commits.body:
InitializeProcThreadAttributeList, UpdateProcThreadAttribute and
DeleteProcThreadAttributeList are now resolved by InitializeSpecificUnit, as
the other Vista+ kernel32 functions, instead of at first use with no lock.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: test: TTestCoreBase._RunRedirect expects fewer signals - see #648
commits.body:
The sender thread of MacOS arm64 GitHub runners sleeps about 100ms instead of
20ms, so only 9 or 10 signals were sent during the 1 second command.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: TExternalProcess child closes descriptors up to the highest opened - see #648
commits.body:
Without closefrom() nor close_range(), e.g. on MacOS or Linux < 5.9, the child
process looped up to RLIMIT_NOFILE, which TPollSockets raises to the hard limit:
one RunRedirect() took 118ms with 524288 descriptors and 230ms with 1048576 on
Linux, instead of 1.3ms - and 33ms instead of 6ms on a MacOS x86_64 runner with
46080 descriptors.
Unless close_range() is available, the parent now lists /proc/self/fd or
/dev/fd before fork(), and the child loops up to the highest descriptor, with
a margin of 64 for the descriptors opened meanwhile by other threads.
A new regression test checks that a descriptor far above all the others is
not inherited.
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: TExternalProcess Windows implementation - see #648
commits.body:
- CreateProcessW() with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, so that each child
  inherits only its own handles - with a lock as fallback before Vista
- the process is created suspended in its own process group and job, so that
  Terminate() sends CTRL_BREAK and WM_QUIT, then stops the whole job, as the
  process group on POSIX
- roWinJobCloseChildren keeps the CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB fallback of
  mormot.ext.os when the current job forbids breakaway
- the background thread peeks and reads the stdout/stderr anonymous pipes,
  and is woken by an event
- Start() with an array of arguments quotes them as CommandLineToArgvW() expects
- RunRedirect() still uses RunCommandWin() on Windows
- Windows regression tests, including the inheritance of handles
commits.author: zen010101

commits.subject: core: new TExternalProcess class with redirected stdin/stdout/stderr - see #648
commits.body:
- one background thread per instance reads stdout/stderr in blocking mode,
  then calls OnOutput/OnError or fills the ReadAvailable/ReadErrorAvailable
  buffers; Destroy terminates the process and waits for this thread
- Start() from a command line, parsed by ParseCommandArgs() as RunRedirect()
  does, or from an array of arguments with no parsing nor shell call
- new roStdinNull/roStdinPipe/roStderrMerge/roStderrPipe options, and
  RUN_PROCESS with the same defaults on all systems: no stdin, stderr in stdout
- POSIX: close-on-exec pipes (pipe2 on Linux), the child closes all other
  descriptors (close_range on Linux 5.9+, closefrom on BSD), restores SIGPIPE
  and its signal mask, and reports an execve() failure so that Start() returns
  false; a lock protects waitpid() and the signals to the process group
- POSIX RunRedirect() is now implemented over this class from the calling
  thread, with the same behavior, plus the roStdinNull/roStderrMerge options
- Windows implementation is pending: Start() returns false by now
- regression tests of RunRedirect(), including the #647 ones, and of
  TExternalProcess
commits.author: zen010101
